messages:
alex: Quick note — the current flow (admit -> select route -> fallback) is producing weird oversubscribe races when admission windows overlap across regions. Seen it twice in prod last week. Thoughts?

maria: This is the window-race I hit when testing soft slots. Two policy-engine replicas accept soft slots for the same tenant, both fall back later, and we end up oversubscribed. Short thread but real.

samir: Can you paste a minimal repro or the policy snippet you used?

maria: Sure — here's a simplified policy we used:
```
admit if tenant_budget > 0 and latency_target <= 100ms
route_priority = cost_weight * 0.7 + latency_score * 0.3
on_no_capacity: fallback("region:b", tier: "burst")
```
This shows where the fallback is decided after admit in our current runtime.

jia: Idea: move fallback decision into the admission phase so that admission returns (chosen_route, fallback_token) atomically. If the admission state is mutated atomically, replicas can't partially accept then fallback. But it requires some form of optimistic locking or compare-and-swap on the admission state.

alex: Tradeoffs: stronger serialization gives correctness but can hurt tail latency. Optimistic locks means retries on contention — we measured ~5-10ms median extra in a microbenchmark. Is that acceptable?

ops-bot: @alex FYI we're seeing a small uptick in admission retries on the staging cluster.

samir: Alternative: deterministic single-shard admission per request key. Hash by (tenant_id, route_name) -> admission-shard. That keeps admission cheap and consistent but centralizes traffic for hot tenants.

maria: Hot-tenant hotspot is my worry. We can mitigate by striping (tenant, route, time-window) or dynamic shard-reshard, but complexity rises.

jia: Another pattern: admit-token. Admission grants a short-lived token the runtime must present when allocating the actual GPU slot. Token expiry is short (e.g., 50-200ms). This decouples logical admission from physical scheduling but prevents double-alloc if runtime enforces single-use tokens.

alex: Compatibility plan? Propose: 1) add admit-token primitive to runtime API (opt-in), 2) expose on_no_capacity hint in DSL so policy authors can opt into token flow, 3) implement optimistic-lock + token hybrid in policy-engine v2 next sprint. Objections?

samir: Metrics needed before rollout: token_issue_rate, token_expiry_rate, token_reject_rate, admission_retry_rate, fallback_hotpath_count. Also run loadgen sim at 10k qps with hot tenants.

maria: +1. I'll write a small simulator and add it to the policy-engine test harness. Also update the rollout checklist with canary thresholds and kill-switch flags.

jia: One more operational note: when serializing fallback, include region-affinity TTL (default 30s) to avoid oscillation between fallbacks across rapid retries.

alex: Sounds good. I'll open a follow-up RFC PR with design sketches, proto changes, rollout plan and testing matrix. Assigning follow-ups: @maria -> sim + tests, @samir -> telemetry dashboard, @jia -> runtime token API.

deploy-bot: canary deploy started for policy-engine v2 (staging) — 2/2 pods healthy

alex: Thanks — we'll sync in architecture sync on Friday to finalize the RFC timeline.
